question: What signals predict whether a sales rep will hit quota in 12 months?
answer:
**Three early signals (month 1–3 ramp): (1) pipeline build velocity ($3k–$5k new pipeline per week by week 4), (2) discovery call discipline (4+ calls per day, documented in CRM), (3) first deal close by month 5 (even small, shows sales mechanics work). Reps hitting these 3 signals have 70%+ quota attainment probability; miss 2+ signals = <30% hit rate.** Pipeline and process are predictors; quota attainment is the trailing outcome. **Why These Signals Work:** 1. **Pipeline velocity predicts quota velocity:** A rep building $3.5k pipeline/week × 13 weeks (quarter) = $45.5k quarterly pipeline. At 20% close rate (typical), that's $9k quarterly closes × 4 quarters = $36k ARR. If quota is $40k, rep is on track to 90% attainment. Miss pipeline targets by week 8, rep will miss quota by week 40. 2. **Discovery call discipline predicts win rate:** Reps logging 4+ discovery calls/day consistently hit 25%+ win rates (vs. 10–15% for lazy callers). More conversations = more opportunities = higher odds one converts. 3. **First deal close by month 5 shows process works:** Month 1–3 is flailing (learning product, territory, ICP). Month 4–5 first deal is proof that the rep, company, and market are aligned. Close nothing by month 6 = rep is likely broken hire. **Early Prediction Scorecard (Month 1–3):** | Signal | Target | Likelihood of 100% Quota Hit | |---|---|---| | All 3 signals | Good pipeline + calls + coach feedback | 70–80% | | 2 of 3 signals | Pipeline or calls weak; compensation? | 40–50% | | 1 of 3 signals | Only one signal present; alarm | 15–20% | | 0 of 3 signals | No pipeline, no calls, no close | <5% | **SIGNAL #1: Pipeline Build Velocity (Week 1–4 Ramp)** **Definition:** New opportunities added to pipeline per week (dollar amount of deal size) **Benchmark:** - **Week 1:** $1k–$2k (new rep, still learning territory) - **Week 2–3:** $2k–$4k (ramping; prospecting) - **Week 4+:** $3k–$5k sustained (should hit this by end of month 1) **How to Measure:** In CRM, filter: "Opportunities created by rep X in the last 7 days, stage = Discovery or later." Sum the ARR of those opportunities. **Why it Works:** - A rep adding $3k pipeline/week has 52 weeks × $3k = $156k pipeline annually - At 25% conversion (typical for mid-market), that's $39k ARR closed annually - If quota is $40k, rep is on track - If rep only builds $1k/week pipeline, they'll never hit quota **Red Flag:** Pipeline velocity flat at $500k–$1k by week 4 = rep is not prospecting. Churn by month 6 likely. **SIGNAL #2: Discovery Call Volume + CRM Discipline (Week 1–4)** **Definition:** Number of documented discovery calls (15–30 min minimum) with prospects; logged in CRM **Benchmark:** - **Target:** 4+ discovery calls per day, 20 calls per week minimum - **Quality gate:** Each call must be logged in CRM with notes (not just call log) **Example Weekly View (Good Rep):** | Day | Calls Logged | Notes | CRM Entry | |---|---|---|---| | Monday | 4 | "Discussed budget, timeline, pain point: scaling support team" | Opportunity created | | Tuesday | 5 | 4 calls = new opps; 1 existing follow-up | Updated 4 opportunities | | Wednesday | 4 | "Found buying signal on 2 calls, created opps" | 2 new opportunities | | Thursday | 3 | Holiday/light day | 3 logged | | Friday | 4 | "Wrapped up week, queued 5 for next week" | 4 logged | | **Weekly Total** | **20** | | | **Red Flag:** Rep logs 5 calls/week but 0 opportunity creations by week 3 = calls are not triggering discovery or pipeline. Either (a) wrong ICP prospected, (b) rep not qualifying, or (c) product not resonating. **Why it Works:** Reps making 20+ discovery calls/week have 3–4 weeks of pipeline visibility. Even if only 10% of calls create opps, that's 2 new opps/week = 8/month = 96/year. At 25% close rate, that's 24 closes. If ACV is $2k, that's $48k ARR = quota attainment. Reps making 5 calls/week will never hit quota. **SIGNAL #3: First Deal Close by Month 5 (Execution Proof)** **Definition:** Closing a deal (any size, even small) by end of month 5 **Why Month 5 Specifically?** - Months 1–2: Onboarding, learning territory, not expected to close - Months 3–4: Building pipeline, early sales conversations, still ramping - Month 5: Rep should have 1–2 closes (even if small, $5k–$10k each) to prove sales mechanics work - Month 6+: If zero closes, rep is not executing on opportunity pipeline or ICP is broken **Example:** - Month 1–4: Rep builds $45k pipeline (signal 1), makes 75 calls (signal 2), creates 8 opportunities - Month 5: Rep closes 1 opportunity ($8k deal), books 2 more for month 6 - **Signal 3 hit:** Proof rep can close - **Probability of quota hit: High (70%+)** VS. - Month 1–4: Rep builds $45k pipeline, makes 75 calls, creates 8 opportunities - Month 5: Rep closes $0, books 0 new opps, loses 2 old opps to competitors - **Signal 3 fail:** Proof rep cannot close - **Probability of quota hit: Very low (<10%)** **Coaching the Weak Signal #3 Rep:** If rep has strong signals 1 & 2 but fails signal 3 by month 5: 1. **Audit discovery calls:** Are they pre-qualified? Or just phone fills? 2. **Audit close conversations:** Is rep even attempting close? Or just gathering info indefinitely? 3. **Audit product fit:** Is ICP wrong? Is pricing uncompetitive? 4. **Audit peer learning:** Pair rep with top performer for 2 weeks of "close ride-alongs" If rep still has zero closes by month 6, likelihood of quota attainment drops below 20%. Plan exit or role change. **The Composite Score (Month 3 Prediction Model):** | Rep | Pipeline Velocity | Calls/Week | First Deal? | Prediction | |---|---|---|---|---| | Alice | $4k/week | 18 calls | Not yet | 65% quota hit | | Bob | $2k/week | 12 calls | Yes ($8k) | 45% quota hit | | Carol | $500/week | 4 calls | No | 8% quota hit | | David | $3.5k/week | 20 calls | Yes ($15k) | 75% quota hit | **CRO Playbook (Managing Prediction):** 1. **Month 1–2:** Monitor pipeline velocity. Coach prospecting. If <$1.5k/week by week 3, escalate training. 2. **Month 3:** Check CRM call discipline. If <12 calls/week, rep is coasting; have manager intervention. 3. **Month 4–5:** Pressure test on first close. If still $0 by month 5, start transition/exit planning. 4. **Month 6:** Evaluate quota trajectory. If on pace for <60% attainment, make role change decision. **Alternative Signals (Weaker Predictors):** - **Education/pedigree:** Comes from strong company (Salesforce, HubSpot). Statistically better close rates (60–70% quota attainment vs. 50% baseline), but not predictive in first 3 months. - **Demo count:** Doesn't predict quota; pipeline predicts quota. Rep can book 30 demos and close 0 deals (no discovery discipline). - **Manager rating:** Subjective. "Rep is a culture fit" doesn't predict sales performance. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[New Rep Hired] --> B[Week 1-4: Build Pipeline] B --> C{Pipeline ≥ $3k/week?} C -->|Yes| D[Signal 1: PASS] C -->|No| E[Signal 1: FAIL] A --> F[Week 1-4: Calls] F --> G{Calls ≥ 16/week?} G -->|Yes| H[Signal 2: PASS] G -->|No| I[Signal 2: FAIL] A --> J[Month 5: First Close] J --> K{Close ≥ $5k?} K -->|Yes| L[Signal 3: PASS] K -->|No| M[Signal 3: FAIL] D --> N{All 3 PASS?} H --> N L --> N N -->|3/3| O["70%+ Quota Hit
